rationale: Abstract noun ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲃⲉⲍⲉ. Etymology unclear; possibly Lyc form related to ⲃⲱⲱⲛ 'wicked' or to ⲃⲏϫⲉ 'lack.' Context (Mani 'humbling their X' before subduing their powers) requires a negative moral-state noun. Tentative.
Verb in line 14 paired with ⲕⲓⲙ 'move' as doublet of immovability. Likely Lyc reflex of ⲕⲱⲧⲡ̄/ϫⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'turn aside, overthrow.' Confidence low; flagged for parallel attestations.

proposed_english: laying-bare of heart / openness of heart
rationale: Compound: ⲕⲱⲕ ('strip, lay bare,' cf. glossary ⲕⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲏⲩ 'strip naked') + ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧ ('of heart'). Distinct from ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲧ 'purpose of heart' in glossary; this expression preserves the 'stripping/laying-bare' image, suggesting candor or sincere disclosure. Used here of how the Medes/Parthians responded to Mani's preaching. Confidence moderate.

Lyc nominal/infinitival form related to ϩⲱⲃ 'work' or ϩⲃⲁ 'subjection.' In context 'has power for ⲉϩⲃ̄ under the kings,' denotes the great Assyrian land's capacity to bear the imperial administrative structure. Confidence moderate.
Lyc reflex of ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ 'he said.' Already attested in accumulated vocabulary; reaffirmed here in line 26 as the standard discourse-introducer.
